question: I bought two bicycles for ₹1,200. I sold the first one at a loss of 10% and the second at a gain of 20%. If, on the whole I made neither a loss nor a gain, find the cost price (in ₹) of the first bicycle.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

By using the mixture and alligation method for the profit and loss percentages:

Ratio of CP of 1st to 2ⁿd bicycle = (Gain% − Net%) : (Net% − Loss%) = (20 − 0) : (0 − (−10)) = 20 : 10 = 2 : 1

Total ratio parts = 2 + 1 = 3 parts = ₹1200 ⇒ 1 part = ₹1200 ÷ 3 = ₹400

Cost price of the 1st bicycle (2 parts) = 2 × ₹400 = ₹800

**∴ The correct answer is ₹800.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total cost price of two bicycles = ₹1200

Loss on the 1st bicycle = 10%

Gain on the 2ⁿd bicycle = 20%

Net profit or loss = 0%
